raw_case_text:
A 76-year-old Japanese woman presented to our hospital because of anorexia. She had a history of advanced right breast cancer, and a total right mastectomy with right axillary lymph node dissection was performed 25 years ago without additional chemotherapy or adjuvant radiation therapy. Seventeen months before presentation, she was diagnosed with a follicular lymphoma that transformed to a diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (t-FL). According to Ann Arbor classification, the tumor was clinically staged as IVA because the patient presented with multiple sites of nodal and extranodal involvement and diffuse skin involvement of thorax and multiple lymph nodes (neck, axilla, and mediastinum). The patient had received six cycles of R-CHOP for 5 months and was recorded as having complete remission once. Four months later, her disease relapsed with multiple mass lesions in the left breast. A fine-needle aspiration biopsy specimen from the tumor confirmed the recurrence of lymphoma; therefore, the patient received four cycles of B-R regimen every 3 weeks and achieved complete remission.
After completion of the B-R regimen, lymphopenia had continued over 3 months (Figure 1). During this time, the patient gradually lost her appetite and had gastrointestinal discomfort. To perform supportive care and to investigate the cause of anorexia, she was admitted again with peripheral blood lymphopenia of 385/muL. Esophagogastroscopy revealed polynesic white protrusions with shallow ulcers in the mid-esophagus (Figure 2A and B). These lesions were diagnosed as HE because several squamous cells had intranuclear inclusion bodies of Cowdry's Type A (Figure 2C), and these cells were positively stained by anti-herpes simplex virus antibody (Figure 2D).
Oral administration of valacyclovir (1,000 mg/d) was initiated as an antiviral treatment. Although appetite loss and gastrointestinal discomfort were relieved in 2 weeks, she developed severe interstitial pneumonia. Since CMV antigenemia test (C7-HRP) was positive (15 of 50,000 white blood cells), ganciclovir (500 mg/d) was administered intravenously. Unfortunately, she passed away because of CMV pneumonia without t-FL relapse.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 76-year-old Japanese woman presented with progressive anorexia and gastrointestinal discomfort persisting for 3 months after completing bendamustine-rituximab chemoimmunotherapy for relapsed transformed follicular lymphoma.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Diagnosed 17 months prior with stage IVA follicular lymphoma transformed to diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (t-FL; treated with 6 cycles of R-CHOP achieving first CR, followed 4 months later by left breast relapse treated with 4 cycles of bendamustine-rituximab [B-R] every 3 weeks achieving second CR), the patient experienced persistent peripheral blood lymphopenia over the 3 months following B-R completion accompanied by progressive loss of appetite and upper gastrointestinal discomfort, prompting hospital readmission.
subjective.past_medical_history: Stage IVA transformed follicular lymphoma (t-FL) in second complete remission status post 6 cycles of R-CHOP and 4 cycles of bendamustine-rituximab (B-R); advanced right breast cancer treated 25 years prior with total right mastectomy and axillary lymph node dissection without chemo/radiotherapy.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for progressive anorexia and gastrointestinal discomfort; subsequently developed severe dyspnea/interstitial pneumonia after 2 weeks of hospitalization.

objective.routine_investigations: Persistent severe peripheral blood lymphopenia for >3 months post-B-R (admission absolute lymphocyte count 385/uL). Two weeks after admission, peripheral blood CMV pp65 antigenemia assay (C7-HRP) was positive at 15 positive cells per 50,000 WBCs.
objective.advanced_workup: Admission esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD) revealed multiple discrete white mucosal protrusions with shallow ulcers in the mid-esophagus; esophageal mucosal biopsy demonstrated squamous epithelial cells with Cowdry type A intranuclear inclusion bodies and positive anti-herpes simplex virus (HSV) immunohistochemistry, confirming herpes esophagitis (HE). Two weeks later, chest imaging and clinical evaluation demonstrated severe interstitial pneumonia.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Diagnosed with bendamustine-rituximab-induced prolonged CD4/lymphocyte depletion (ALC 385/uL) complicated sequentially by biopsy-proven herpes simplex virus (HSV) esophagitis (confirmed by Cowdry type A intranuclear inclusions and positive anti-HSV IHC on mid-esophageal biopsy) and fatal cytomegalovirus (CMV) interstitial pneumonia (confirmed by positive C7-HRP CMV antigenemia of 15/50,000 WBCs). Oral valacyclovir (1,000 mg/day) resolved the anorexia and HSV esophagitis within 2 weeks, and intravenous ganciclovir (500 mg/day) was initiated for CMV pneumonia; however, the patient died of severe CMV pneumonia while in complete lymphoma remission.
